title: Traffic mirroring + sequential stat-check runner for phased model adoption
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need a low-friction way to validate model versions using both mirrored (shadow) traffic and synthetic canaries, with automated, signal-driven stop/rollback and clear human override. Existing experiment tooling focuses on exposure scheduling and cohort splits but lacks a unified runner that: (1) supports traffic mirroring with sampling rules and per-tenant scopes, (2) runs sequential statistical checks (alpha spending / early stop) across multiple metrics, and (3) wires automated rollback triggers to the rollout controller while preserving an audit trail and operator approval flow.

Proposal: Build a stat-check runner service and console UX that coordinates mirrored traffic ingestion, synthetic-canary generators, metric ingestion and sequential hypothesis tests, and a webhook-driven rollback/fallback API. The runner will be configurable per-experiment with policies for exposure cap, statistical thresholds, minimum sample sizes, and grace periods. We will ship an initial beta with a limited set of metrics: request latency p95, error rate, model-token cost delta, and an evaluation quality signal derived from prompt-based checks (synthetic ground-truth prompts).
acceptance_criteria: Console: create + configure experiment with: traffic mirroring toggle, synthetic canary template, exposure schedule (percentages over time), and per-metric thresholds.
Runtime: runner ingests mirrored requests and synthetic canaries, emits metrics to observability pipeline, and evaluates sequential tests at configured intervals.
Safety: automated rollback webhook triggers when preconfigured multi-metric failure conditions are met; operator can opt to pause/override via Console UI.
Observability: per-cohort dashboards with time-series of each metric, sample counts, and p-value / confidence interval evolution plots.
Docs & runbook: runbook for setting conservative alpha spending, minimum sample sizes, and post-rollback investigation steps.
Integration: end-to-end test against a non-production cluster, and a staged canary with an internal partner team (integration sign-off).
success_metrics: Reduce manual rollback events by 30% for partner canaries in first quarter after launch.
Achieve 90%+ confidence in early-stop decisions while keeping false-positive rollback rate below 1% on historical benchmarks.
Onboard 3 internal teams to beta within 6 weeks of release.
Mean time from automated trigger to operator acknowledgement < 10 minutes for enabled PagerDuty channels.
technical_notes: Sequential test engine: initial implementation will use alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) to allow multiple looks without inflating type-I error. Consider Group Sequential and Bayesian alternatives after beta.
Metrics pipeline: use existing metrics ingestion (Prometheus + metrics service) and an evaluation job that computes p-values and effect sizes on windowed slices.
Traffic mirroring: extend router to support mirroring rules by route, region, and customer namespace with sampling fraction; mirrored requests must not count against customer rate limits.
Synthetic canaries: templated prompt/trace generator stored in Console; runner replays at configurable cadence and tags results for experiment correlation.
Rollback API: webhook POST to rollout controller with structured reason, metric state, and suggested rollback window; controller must log events and support immediate and scheduled rollback.
Data privacy: mirrored payloads are redacted per privacy policy; PII scrubbing and KMS-encrypted artifact storage for synthetic-ground-truth records.
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: finalize spec and acceptance criteria; design Console UX mockups and experiment DSL for exposure schedules.
Week 3-4: implement runner skeleton, mirroring hook in router, and synthetic canary store; unit tests for mirroring sampling behavior.
Week 5-6: integrate metrics ingestion and sequential test logic; build initial dashboard visualizations and alert rules.
Week 7: rollout controller integration and webhook-based rollback logic; implement operator override flows in Console.
Week 8: internal alpha with platform team; iterate on thresholds and sample-size defaults based on observed variance.
Week 9-10: documentation, runbook, security review, and beta launch for 3 partner teams.
